history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 741 ("Dimapur Kalibari", id dimapur-kalibari) - same real temple; unique id used here. Dimapur Kalibari is the well-documented Kali temple of Dimapur, Nagaland, on Kalibari Road in Railway Colony / West Yard Colony (coordinates 25.9043 N, 93.7253 E per Wikipedia). The present temple was built in 1956 with major contributions from local philanthropists J.C. Das and M.M. Mazumder and other devotees; it celebrated its golden jubilee in 2006 with the launch of community services including an ambulance service and a library. It is one of the more famous Hindu temples in Northeast India and a spiritual centre of the Bengali Hindu community in Nagaland.

name: Dimapur Kalibari
town_description: Dimapur is Nagaland's largest city and its commercial hub, and the main gateway into the state. It sits at the foothills of the Naga Hills in Dimapur district and is home to the state's only civil airport and a key railway station. The town is known for the medieval Kachari Rajbari ruins and its mix of Naga and non-Naga communities.

travel.road: On Kalibari Road, West Yard Colony, Railway Colony; accessible by auto-rickshaw from the city centre

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (pleasant weather, 15-25°C); Durga Puja (Sep-Oct) and Kali Puja (Oct-Nov) for the biggest celebrations
